newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber futures close down $10 limit.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber futures close down $10 limit.

text.p: CME March lumber futures closed down the $10.00 per tbf daily limit on local and commercial pressure prompted by continued slower-than-expected cash market activity, traders said.
March closed limit down at $412.80 per thousand board feet while limitless January finished $6.60 lower at $412.40 per tbf. Other months ended $6.50 lower to $2.00 higher.

"We came into the year with a lot of optimism and no business and the no business finally caught up with the optimism," said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures, referring to the selling that took CME futures limit down.
Mills have been hedging in futures which showed that post-holiday movement of lumber was not as active as had been expected, cash sources said.

Selling by Saul Stone added to pressure from a large local which pushed March down into sell stops. There were about 60 contracts still being offered at the close in March which should weigh on prices early Friday, traders added.
